result.title: EARS: Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and Motion for Budgeted Video Reasoning
result.summary: Uniform frame sampling can miss brief evidence in sparse-event videos when the VLM sees only K frames. We propose EARS (Evidence-Aware Retrieval via Sound and motion), a training-free, query-free front-end that ranks frames using optical-flow motion and audio energy, then applies temporal non-maximum suppression for diversity. The evidence score alone has frame-level AP 0.39; used only to select frames for the VLM, EARS with temporal diversity reaches localization AP 0.94, compared with 0.88 under Uniform sampling. In the updated matched study, at K = 1 EARS reaches XD-subset F1 0.660 versus 0.614 for centered Uniform (the paired interval includes zero); earlier backbone studies use separate protocols. On mostly-silent UCF-Crime, however, EARS slightly trails Uniform. A single configuration is used across both benchmarks; the new controls do not repeat the original held-out search. EARS therefore targets low-budget videos whose salient evidence aligns with motion or audio; on dense narratives or stealthy events, uniform or semantic selection remains preferable, and cheap modality statistics cannot reliably route between them. Code: https://github.com/mikeslin-ir/EARS

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EARS：一个免训练、免查询的前端，用光流运动能量与音频能量为视频帧打分，再做时间非极大值抑制保证多样性，从而在仅取 K 帧的低预算下为 VLM 挑选证据帧，并在稀疏事件视频上对比均匀采样报告定位与 F1 结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「视觉证据筛选」与 LOOK 预算问题，作者也报告了稠密叙事、静音视频上劣于均匀采样、廉价模态统计无法可靠路由的负结果，可供核查阈值式证据选择与模态统计路由的适用边界；但方法停留在模型外部的前端挑帧，不涉及内部状态或 latent 推理。
